requests.prompt:
Create one production-oriented animation sheet for the SAME three-head-tall hand-painted 2D adventurer, grounded sword attack number 1. Image 1 is the exact identity/style reference. Image 2 is a measured scale-and-ground-root template of this same accepted character. Preserve the same tousled dark-brown hair, large brown eye, face proportions, skin tone, warm ochre tunic, brown leather shoulder and belt, blue-gray wrapped wrists, short charcoal trousers, brown boots, thick dark ink outlines and restrained cel shading. Keep the fixed 3/4-facing-right side-scroller camera seen in the references in every frame. No new costume, no front-facing face, no changing head size, no pixel art.

Output a wide 1536x1024 sheet with exactly TWO ROWS and THREE COLUMNS of equal invisible 512x512 cells. Six full-body poses in reading order, one continuous sword-slash action only. Solid flat #FF00FF magenta background everywhere outside the character, no gradients, no floor, no baked shadow, no text, no labels, no grid lines, no borders, no separated motion effects. Keep a fixed standing-equivalent anatomical height about414px per source cell, matching Image2 rather than resizing each pose. Feet rest on the same local y466 ground line; body/pelvis centered around x256. Keep all limbs in the central70% width, retain magenta padding on all four sides. This established height is intentional to match the current game. Bend knees/rotate torso naturally without translating or zooming the whole body. All hair, hands and boots fully visible; no crossing cell boundaries.

BODY ONLY: absolutely no sword, blade, hilt, shield, slash trail or detached effect drawn into these frames. A separate sword sprite will be attached later. Nevertheless the near/right hand must unmistakably GRIP an imaginary cylindrical sword handle: thumb wraps across the curled fingers, knuckles curve around the cylinder, wrist forms the correct sword-grasp axis. Use the same closed sword grip throughout, never an open reaching palm. Do not make a punch or straight forward jab. The shoulder, torso, elbow and wrist must trace a large curved diagonal CUT, not push the fist forward along a horizontal line. The nonweapon hand balances behind/near the torso and never overlaps or replaces the grip hand.

Six poses, two anticipation + two cutting + two recovery:
1 top-left: right sword-grip hand drawn behind and beside the head at shoulder/head height, elbow bent, chest coiled slightly away, eyes still toward screen-right; balanced grounded stance.
2 top-middle: stronger backswing, right grip behind the upper head, elbow raised, shoulders visibly rotate back, knees compress slightly. The hand is holding a handle, not winding up a boxing jab.
3 top-right: begin the downward diagonal slash by rotating the chest toward screen-right; bent elbow leads the gripping wrist across the upper front of the body near face/chest height. Wrist angle implies a blade sweeping forward-down from overhead, not a straight arm thrust.
4 bottom-left: decisive low-front diagonal follow-through; right grip travels in an arc to low screen-right near the waist/thigh, torso rotates through, elbow is softly bent, right wrist pivots downward. Both boots remain in the same rooted ground area.
5 bottom-middle: finish the cut low across the front, elbow folding back toward body, body unwinds with grounded weight and visible shoulder rotation.
6 bottom-right: return to compact low sword guard with the same closed right grip and stable footing, ready to transition to an opposite-direction second slash.

Make the anticipation, cutting and recovery visibly different poses with real torso twist and wrist rotation. No motion blur, no smear limbs, no duplicate arms, no boxing pose, no forward-punch series. Preserve the character's standing-equivalent head/torso/limb dimensions and fixed camera exactly. Do not reproduce the neutral template poses; it is only the numeric scale/root guide.

Frame5 bottom-middle: high follow-through, gripping wrist settles inward toward the near shoulder while the torso unwinds and knees return to neutral. Do not repeat frame4 unchanged.
Frame6 bottom-right: compact high sword guard near shoulder/chest height, same closed grip, ready to load an overhead finishing cut. Ground contact and anatomy match frame1.

Two anticipation frames, two active rising-cut frames, two recovery frames. Distinct physical poses, coherent identity and strong shoulder/wrist rotation.
